about.title: Personal Injury Help in Rancho Cucamonga, California
about.longDescription: Rancho Cucamonga sits where the 210 and the 15 cross paths, and much of daily life here moves along those two freeways or the long stretch of Foothill Boulevard that runs through the heart of town. Public records for 2025 show 474 injury collisions in the city, with 649 people hurt and 6 lives lost. Reports tend to climb on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters heading home from across San Bernardino County share the road with shoppers and families. SR-210, Foothill Boulevard, and I-15 carry the highest collision counts in the city's public data. A crash is only one way people get hurt here, though. Slips in a store aisle, a dog that bites without warning, a fall at a rental, or a bicycle struck near a Victoria Gardens parking lot can each leave someone facing medical bills and missed work. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases in the Inland Empire, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case results in a recovery. You talk through what happened; the attorney tells you where things stand.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Rancho Cucamonga Claim

items.title: Two years is the usual window
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within 2 years of the injury. Claims against a city, county, or state agency can require notice in as little as 6 months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you were partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by your share of the blame rather than wiped out.

items.title: No fixed ceiling on pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: You pay nothing unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency. Their fee comes out of any recovery, and if there is none, you owe them no fee.

items.question: Where do collisions in Rancho Cucamonga tend to cluster?
items.answer: Public collision records list SR-210 (Foothill Freeway), Foothill Boulevard, and I-15 (Ontario Freeway) as the corridors with the highest counts in the city. These are simply the roads carrying the most traffic and the most reported crashes. Reports also rise on Fridays between roughly 5 p.m. and 7 p.m.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury cases, the deadline is 2 years from the date you were hurt. If a government entity is involved, such as a city vehicle or a hazard on public property, you may need to file a claim within 6 months. An attorney can confirm which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means your compensation is reduced by your percentage of responsibility but not eliminated. Being 30 percent at fault, for example, would reduce your recovery by 30 percent. You can still pursue a claim.
